title: The Big Freeze
briefing: Case study, inspired by the 2021 Texas winter storm. A week of -18C cold has hit the region and the grid operator has started rolling blackouts of up to 20 hours.
For a cold chain the danger runs the other way: medicines that must stay between 2 and 8C can freeze. Amara Lindqvist asks you to check whether Harrowgate can ride it out on its generator.

evidence.title: Harrowgate backup generator
body: Fuel tank: 400 litres, full. Consumption at the current load: 25 litres an hour.

evidence.title: Grid operator notice
evidence.body: Rolling outages of up to 20 hours at a time, possibly repeated over five days. Road fuel deliveries are delayed by ice.

evidence.title: Stored product
evidence.body: 1.2 million of temperature-sensitive vaccines in the Harrowgate chilled store. Freezing below 0C destroys them.

questions.prompt: How many hours can the Harrowgate generator run on a full tank?

mistakes.feedback: 20 hours is the length of the outage, not what the tank lasts.

questions.prompt: How many extra litres of fuel are needed to cover one 20-hour outage?
questions.explanation: The outage outlasts the tank by 4 hours; 4 x 25 = 100 litres.

options.label: Pre-position winter-grade diesel on site, keep trucks' heaters running and agree priority fuel delivery
options.feedback: It closes the fuel gap, removes the summer-diesel gelling risk and protects the vaccines.

options.label: Move all the vaccines to another site with a stable grid
options.feedback: Moving 1.2 million of vaccines in ice is a risk of its own, and no site is guaranteed a stable grid.

options.label: Check the insurance covers freezing losses
options.feedback: Worth knowing, but it does not stop the loss or the patients' shortage.

options.label: Monitor temperatures and react if they fall
options.feedback: By the time the store freezes it is too late; this needs action before the outage.

questions.prompt: Which risks does extreme cold create for a cold chain? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Chilled products freezing
options.feedback: The headline risk: 2-8C products are destroyed below 0C.

options.label: Summer-grade diesel gelling in generators and trucks
options.feedback: Summer diesel waxes in deep cold and stops engines.

options.label: Staff unable to reach sites safely
Customers no longer needing refrigeration
options.feedback: Medicines still need 2-8C whatever the weather outside.

questions.prompt: Rate a multi-day winter grid failure at a key cold store, before treatment.
questions.explanation: Rare in this climate (unlikely), but losing a store of vaccines is catastrophic (severe).

lesson: Resilience is arithmetic before it is heroics: fuel hours against outage hours. Cold-chain risk includes too cold, not only too hot.
